concepts.title: Dark Factory
concepts.description: Self-contained tmux subsystem that runs persistent SAFe agent teams on a headless machine.
concepts.notes: listed inventory: 5 operator scripts in scripts/, 3 team layouts in templates/team-layouts/, 4 docs in docs/, 4 templates (env.template, tmux.conf, codex-factory.sh, github/merge-queue-ruleset.json) | two runtimes: Claude Code (pane-per-agent, driven by factory-start.sh) and Codex CLI (window-per-agent, driven by the standalone codex-factory.sh template) | all state lives under $HOME/.dark-factory: env, logs/<session>/, logs/archive/, worktrees/<session>/agent-N | entry point factory-setup.sh gates on GitHub merge queue enforcement and exits 1 if absent | sessions named factory-<ticket-id> or factory-<timestamp>; every script filters tmux sessions by the literal '^factory-' prefix | NOT distributed by scripts/apply-workflow.sh (that script copies only patterns_library, specs_templates, linting_configs); dark-factory/ appears in .harness-manifest.yml line 161 as a shared path | no CI workflow in .github/workflows references dark-factory | codex-factory.sh is a fill-in-the-blanks template with {{PROJECT_PATH}}/{{TICKET_PREFIX}}/{{TICKET_ID}}/{{TEAM_SIZE}} tokens and is never invoked by factory-start.sh | DOC DRIFT: dark-factory/README.md directory tree labels the layouts '2-3 agent', '4-5 agent', '6-9 agent'; factory-start.sh and the layout scripts hardcode exactly 3, 5, and 9 panes

concepts.title: factory-setup.sh
concepts.description: One-time Dark Factory setup that checks tools, creates ~/.dark-factory, and gates on merge queue.
concepts.notes: set -euo pipefail | takes no arguments | sources $HOME/.dark-factory/env if present to pick up FACTORY_MAIN_BRANCH; if unset MAIN_BRANCH stays the literal unsubstituted {{MAIN_BRANCH}} token and every gh api call below is built from it | checks command -v for exactly: tmux, claude, git, gh; dies listing all missing | mkdir -p $HOME/.dark-factory/logs and /worktrees | copies dark-factory/templates/env.template to $HOME/.dark-factory/env only when that file is absent; warns and continues if the template is missing | readiness gate: gh repo view --json nameWithOwner, then GET repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets, then GET each ruleset by id, parsing with inline python3 heredocs; a ruleset counts when it has a rule of type merge_queue AND its conditions.ref_name.include contains the branch string or '~DEFAULT_BRANCH' | fallback: GET repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<branch>/protection and treat a non-null 'required_merge_queue' key as proof | second gate: grep -rl merge_group over $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.github/workflows/*.yml | if either gate fails, prints READINESS GATE FAILED and exit 1 | warns (does not fail) when CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS is unset | exit codes: 0 success, 1 missing tools / unresolvable repo / gate failure | hard runtime dependency on python3 for all JSON parsing, but python3 is NOT in the command -v prerequisite loop and NOT in the prerequisite tables in README.md or DARK-FACTORY-GUIDE.md | contains a dead code block: a python3 heredoc guarded by 'if False' whose result is discarded by 'if ...; then true; fi' | DOC DRIFT: env.template labels FACTORY_MERGE_METHOD and FACTORY_REQUIRE_QUEUE 'do not change -- enforced by factory-setup.sh'; factory-setup.sh never reads either variable | DOC DRIFT: gate greps only *.yml, so a merge_group trigger in a *.yaml workflow is invisible

concepts.title: factory-start.sh
concepts.description: Creates a tmux session, optional per-agent worktrees, applies a team layout, and pipes pane logs.
concepts.notes: usage: factory-start.sh <story|feature|epic> [ticket-id]; any other team-size dies | dies if $HOME/.dark-factory/env is missing, telling the operator to run factory-setup.sh | reads keys FACTORY_LOG_DIR, FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES, FACTORY_WORKTREE_DIR, FACTORY_AUTO_ATTACH, FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR from that file, each with an inline fallback | session name is factory-<ticket-id>, or factory-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S) when no ticket is passed; dies if tmux has-session already matches | worktrees are created BEFORE the layout so agents cd into them: pane_count is hardcoded story=3 feature=5 epic=9, and for i in 1..pane_count it runs git worktree add -b <session>-agent-<i> <FACTORY_WORKTREE_DIR>/<session>/agent-<i> <current-branch>, downgrading any failure to an INFO 'may already exist' | declares associative array FACTORY_PANE_WORKDIRS and calls export on it; bash cannot export associative arrays, so this only works because the layout file is sourced into the same shell, not executed | defines and export -f agent_workdir <pane_index>, which returns the worktree path when worktrees are on and FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR otherwise; all three layout scripts call it | starts the session detached with tmux -f dark-factory/templates/tmux.conf when that file exists, plain tmux new-session -d otherwise | sources dark-factory/templates/team-layouts/<team-size>-team.sh, which creates every pane and sends the claude command lines | logging: for each pane, tmux pipe-pane 'cat >> <FACTORY_LOG_DIR>/<session>/<title>.log' where title is lowercased, spaces to dashes, then tr -cd 'a-z0-9_-' — so 'TDM (lead)' becomes 'tdm-lead' | ends with exec tmux attach when FACTORY_AUTO_ATTACH is true | targets window index 1 throughout (matches base-index 1 in tmux.conf); with default tmux settings those targets would not resolve

concepts.title: factory-stop.sh
concepts.description: Interrupts agent panes, kills the session, removes worktrees, and archives per-agent logs.
concepts.notes: usage: factory-stop.sh [session-name]; with no argument it lists sessions matching ^factory- and read -rp prompts, but dies when stdin is not a tty | dies if tmux has-session fails for the named session | sources $HOME/.dark-factory/env if present for FACTORY_LOG_DIR, FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES, FACTORY_WORKTREE_DIR | shutdown: collects pane_id list, tmux send-keys C-c to every pane, then polls once per second for up to 30 seconds using pgrep -P <pane_pid> -f claude to decide whether any agent is still alive | worktree cleanup only when FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES is true: git worktree remove <dir> --force for each agent-* dir, then rmdir the session dir, every failure swallowed with || true | log archive: mv <FACTORY_LOG_DIR>/<session> to <FACTORY_LOG_DIR>/archive/<session>; mv is unguarded, so an existing archive entry for the same session name nests rather than replaces | DOC DRIFT: step 4 is commented 'Kill remaining panes' and the timeout branch prints 'Force-killing remaining panes', but the code only re-sends C-c and sleeps 1; the actual kill is tmux kill-session in step 5 | never SIGKILLs a hung claude process, so an agent ignoring SIGINT is terminated only as a side effect of the session dying

concepts.title: factory-status.sh
concepts.description: Color-coded dashboard classifying every factory pane as active, idle, or dead.
concepts.notes: takes no arguments; exits 0 with 'No dark factory sessions running.' when tmux list-sessions has no ^factory- match | per session prints creation time via date -d @<epoch>, falling back to date -r <epoch>, then 'unknown' | per pane reads pane_index, pane_title, pane_pid, pane_current_command, pane_last_activity | liveness test is pgrep -P <pane_pid> -f claude — it only sees claude as a DIRECT child of the pane shell, so a claude wrapped in another process reads as dead | classification: no claude child = dead (red); claude present and now-pane_last_activity > 300 = idle (yellow); otherwise active (green); the 300-second threshold is hardcoded | aggregate line counts claude processes with pgrep -f claude, which matches any command line containing the substring 'claude' including this script's own greps | RSS total comes from 'ps -C claude -o rss=' summed by awk; -C is a procps/Linux flag that BSD/macOS ps does not support, so on macOS the sum is empty and the dashboard reports ~0MB while still claiming processes exist | no exit code other than 0; it is read-only and never touches tmux state | intended to be wrapped in 'watch -n 5' per README.md

concepts.title: factory-attach.sh
concepts.description: Lists running factory sessions and panes, or attaches to a session and optional pane.
concepts.notes: three modes by argument count | 0 args: lists tmux sessions matching ^factory- and, for each, tmux list-panes showing '[index] title (current_command)'; exits 0 even when nothing is running | 1 arg (session): dies if tmux has-session fails, otherwise exec tmux attach -t <session> | 2 args (session, pane-index): tmux select-pane -t <session>:1.<pane-index>, dies if that fails, then exec tmux attach | window index 1 is hardcoded in the select-pane target, which only resolves because dark-factory/templates/tmux.conf sets base-index 1 and pane-base-index 1 | exec replaces the shell, so nothing runs after attach | does not offer read-only attach; CURSOR-SSH-GUIDE.md tells operators to run 'tmux attach -t <session> -r' directly for that

concepts.title: Story Team Layout
concepts.description: Three-pane tmux layout starting TDM lead, BE Developer, and QAS agents.
concepts.notes: sourced (not executed) by factory-start.sh; depends on SESSION_NAME and the exported agent_workdir function from that script | pane 1 pre-exists from new-session; two splits produce 3 panes total: 1 TDM (lead), 2 BE Developer, 3 QAS | titles set with tmux select-pane -T; unlike the feature and epic layouts there is no re-title pass after the splits | CLAUDE_FLAGS is '--dangerously-skip-permissions' when FACTORY_AUTO_PERMISSIONS is true, empty string otherwise | resolves DIR_1..DIR_3 via agent_workdir | pane 1 gets 'cd <dir> && claude <flags> -p <TDM prompt>' where the prompt instructs the agent to act as team lead, follow the SAFe workflow in CLAUDE.md, create PRs with gh pr create, enqueue with gh pr merge --auto --squash, and never merge directly | panes 2 and 3 get a bare 'cd <dir> && claude <flags>' with no role prompt, so the BE Developer and QAS roles exist only as pane titles | ends by selecting pane 1 | matches the story pane_count=3 branch in factory-start.sh

concepts.title: Feature Team Layout
concepts.description: Five-pane tmux layout starting TDM lead plus BE, FE, QAS, and RTE agents.
concepts.notes: sourced by factory-start.sh; requires SESSION_NAME and agent_workdir | 4 splits on top of the initial pane give 5 panes | the splits assign titles once, then a second re-title pass overwrites them because indices shift during splitting; the final mapping is 1 TDM (lead), 2 BE Developer, 3 QAS, 4 FE Developer, 5 RTE | DOC DRIFT: the ASCII layout comment at the top of the file shows row 2 as BE|FE and row 3 as QAS|RTE, but the final re-title pass puts QAS at index 3 and FE at index 4, so pane titles and the documented grid disagree | CLAUDE_FLAGS is '--dangerously-skip-permissions' only when FACTORY_AUTO_PERMISSIONS is true | only pane 1 receives a -p prompt (TDM lead, PRs via gh pr create, enqueue via gh pr merge --auto --squash, never merge directly); panes 2-5 launch bare claude sessions | ends by selecting pane 1 | matches the feature pane_count=5 branch in factory-start.sh

concepts.title: Epic Team Layout
concepts.description: Nine-pane tmux layout starting the full SAFe agent team led by the TDM.
concepts.notes: sourced by factory-start.sh; requires SESSION_NAME and agent_workdir | 8 splits on top of the initial pane give 9 panes | titles are assigned during splitting and then fully overwritten by an explicit re-title block the file itself labels 'best-effort labels' because indices shift; final mapping is 1 TDM (lead), 2 BSA, 3 BE Developer, 4 QAS, 5 RTE, 6 ARCH, 7 FE Developer, 8 Security, 9 Data Engineer | DOC DRIFT: the ASCII grid comment orders the roles TDM / BSA ARCH Security / BE FE Data / QAS RTE, which does not match the final index-to-role mapping | roles map to the SAFe team: TDM, BSA, ARCH, Security, BE, FE, Data, QAS, RTE | CLAUDE_FLAGS gains --dangerously-skip-permissions when FACTORY_AUTO_PERMISSIONS is true | only pane 1 gets a -p prompt, phrased for 'an epic-level effort', with the same PR-and-merge-queue instructions; panes 2-9 launch bare claude | matches the epic pane_count=9 branch in factory-start.sh, which therefore creates 9 worktrees when worktrees are enabled

concepts.title: Dark Factory Runtime Topology
concepts.description: The tmux, filesystem, and environment-key topology a running Dark Factory session occupies.
concepts.notes: filesystem: $HOME/.dark-factory holds env (copied from templates/env.template), logs/<session>/<agent>.log, logs/archive/<session>/ after stop, worktrees/<session>/agent-N | Codex variant adds $HOME/.codex-yolo/audit.log | tmux.conf settings: default-terminal screen-256color, history-limit 50000, mouse on, status-interval 5, pane-border-status top with pane-border-format '#{pane_title}', allow-rename off and automatic-rename off, monitor-activity on, base-index 1 and pane-base-index 1, Alt+arrow pane switching bound with -n (no prefix), and 'prefix + L' opening a display-popup that tails ~/.dark-factory/logs/<session>/*.log | the base-index 1 setting is load-bearing: every script targets <session>:1.<pane> | env.template KEY NAMES only: FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR, FACTORY_MAIN_BRANCH, FACTORY_TICKET_PREFIX, FACTORY_SSH_KEY, FACTORY_REMOTE_HOST, FACTORY_REMOTE_USER, FACTORY_LOG_DIR, FACTORY_WORKTREE_DIR, FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES, FACTORY_AUTO_PERMISSIONS, FACTORY_AUTO_ATTACH, CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS, FACTORY_MERGE_METHOD, FACTORY_REQUIRE_QUEUE | of those, factory-start.sh reads PROJECT_DIR, LOG_DIR, USE_WORKTREES, WORKTREE_DIR, AUTO_ATTACH; the layouts read AUTO_PERMISSIONS; factory-setup.sh reads MAIN_BRANCH; SSH_KEY, REMOTE_HOST, REMOTE_USER and TICKET_PREFIX are read by no script in dark-factory | Codex topology differs: one tmux WINDOW per agent named after the role plus a 'Control' window tailing the audit log, session named codex-factory-<TICKET_PREFIX>-<TICKET_ID>, requires OPENAI_API_KEY and a .codex/agents/ directory under PROJECT_PATH | remote access is SSH/Cursor Remote-SSH per CURSOR-SSH-GUIDE.md; read-only observation is plain 'tmux attach -r'

concepts.title: Dark Factory Guide
concepts.description: Comprehensive setup, operation, worktree, logging, and troubleshooting guide for the Claude Code factory.
concepts.notes: 485 lines, 14 numbered sections: Overview, Prerequisites, Installation, Starting a Session, Monitoring, Stopping, Git Worktrees, Log Management, Session Durability and Recovery, Security Considerations, Integrating with SAFe Workflow, Companion Tools, Troubleshooting, FAQ | prerequisite table lists tmux 3.0+, Claude Code 2.1+, gh 2.0+, git 2.30+ and claims factory-setup.sh 'validates all prerequisites automatically' | DOC DRIFT: factory-setup.sh additionally requires python3 for every gh api JSON parse and does not check for it, so the table is incomplete and setup can fail after the prerequisite step passes | describes setup as 5 steps matching factory-setup.sh's actual step order | FAQ states tmux sessions are lost on reboot and recommends tmux-resurrect, which the subsystem does not ship or configure | FAQ states Agent Teams is optional and that panes are independent claude instances — consistent with the layouts, which start bare claude in every non-lead pane | quotes ~200-500MB RSS per Claude process and 1-2.5GB for a 5-agent feature team | uses {{MAIN_BRANCH}}, {{GITHUB_ORG}}, {{PROJECT_REPO}} substitution tokens

concepts.title: Merge Queue Policy
concepts.description: The single-path-to-trunk policy: GitHub merge queue with squash, enforced by ruleset not by client flags.
concepts.notes: 227 lines | states one allowed merge command: gh pr merge --auto --squash; all three team layouts embed exactly that string in the TDM prompt | explicitly denies that '--merge-queue' is a real gh option and states enforcement lives in GitHub branch rulesets, not client-side flags | prescribed ruleset: merge queue required on the main branch, merge method squash, max entries 5, 30-minute check timeout, ALLGREEN strategy, strict_required_status_checks_policy false, no bypass actors | ships dark-factory/templates/github/merge-queue-ruleset.json for import via Settings > Rules > Rulesets, with manual UI steps as a fallback | requires CI workflows to carry the merge_group event trigger; factory-setup.sh greps .github/workflows/*.yml for 'merge_group' as half its readiness gate | stop-the-line rule: if the queue is unavailable agents stop creating PRs, the TDM reports the blocker, and there is no fallback to direct merge | squash means the PR title becomes the trunk commit message, so PR titles must match 'type(scope): description [<PREFIX>-XXX]' | monitoring commands: gh pr checks, gh pr list --json number,title,mergeStateStatus, gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/mergequeue | uses {{MAIN_BRANCH}} and {{TICKET_PREFIX}} tokens

concepts.title: Codex Dark Factory Guide
concepts.description: How to run the window-based Codex CLI factory with the third-party codex-yolo auto-approval daemon.
concepts.notes: 421 lines, 12 sections | describes codex-yolo as a third-party daemon that watches tmux capture-pane output for Codex approval prompts, auto-approves writes and command execution, and appends to ~/.codex-yolo/audit.log; positions it as the external equivalent of Claude Code's --dangerously-skip-permissions | prerequisites add Codex CLI, codex-yolo, Node.js 22+ and OPENAI_API_KEY on top of tmux/gh/git | one tmux WINDOW per role because Codex CLI sessions are full-screen, unlike the pane-based Claude factory | roles map to .codex/agents/*.toml configs: tdm, bsa, system-architect, security-engineer, be-developer, fe-developer, data-engineer, qas, rte | notes QAS runs sandbox_mode read-only by design | states codex-yolo is not officially supported by OpenAI and should only run on isolated infrastructure | DOC DRIFT: the FAQ says worktrees are enabled by setting FACTORY_USE_WORKTREES=true in ~/.dark-factory/env and by uncommenting the worktree section in the template; codex-factory.sh never sources ~/.dark-factory/env (it reads the variable from the process environment only) and its worktree block is live code, not commented out | DOC DRIFT: the guide describes launching via codex-factory.sh, but that file is a template whose {{PROJECT_PATH}}, {{TICKET_PREFIX}}, {{TICKET_ID}} and {{TEAM_SIZE}} tokens must be hand-replaced before it will run at all

concepts.title: Cursor SSH Guide
concepts.description: Setting up Cursor Remote-SSH to observe and intervene in a remote Dark Factory session.
concepts.notes: 191 lines | covers ssh config (ForwardAgent yes, ServerAliveInterval 60, ServerAliveCountMax 3), installing the Microsoft Remote - SSH extension in Cursor, connecting, and opening the project folder | observation recipes: factory-status.sh, 'tmux attach -t <session> -r' for read-only, factory-attach.sh <session> <pane> to land in one agent, 'watch -n 5 factory-status.sh', and tail -f over ~/.dark-factory/logs/<session>/*.log | navigation keys documented: prefix+q pane numbers, prefix+o cycle, prefix+z zoom, Alt+arrow move — Alt+arrow is bound with -n in templates/tmux.conf, the others are tmux defaults | recommends git blame to attribute changes to the agent that made them, which works because each worktree commits on its own <session>-agent-N branch | warns about nested tmux keybinding conflicts inside Cursor's terminal and suggests a separate server via 'tmux -L dark-factory' | uses {{REMOTE_USER}}, {{REMOTE_HOST}}, {{SSH_KEY_PATH}}, {{PROJECT_PATH}}, {{TICKET_PREFIX}} tokens whose values live under the FACTORY_SSH_KEY / FACTORY_REMOTE_HOST / FACTORY_REMOTE_USER keys in env.template — keys no script in dark-factory actually reads

concepts.title: Spec Templates
concepts.description: Five SAFe planning and specification templates that drive the spec-first workflow.
concepts.notes: listed contents: 5 markdown files (README, spec_template, planning_template, program_template, pi_planning_template) plus one binary companion pi_planning_template.xlsx | copied wholesale into adopter repos by scripts/apply-workflow.sh lines 93-95 | CLAUDE.md's SAFe workflow makes step 1 'BSA creates spec in specs/<PREFIX>-XXX-feature-spec.md', which is what spec_template.md scaffolds | ownership per README.md: planning_template is BSA-owned for Epic to Feature to Story to Enabler decomposition, pi_planning_template covers a full Program Increment, program_template covers a SAFe x AI-DLC program | none of these files is read by any script; they are copy-and-fill artifacts | DOC DRIFT: two placeholder dialects coexist — planning_template.md and spec_template.md use __TICKET_PREFIX__ double-underscore tokens while program_template.md and pi_planning_template.md use {{TICKET_PREFIX}} brace tokens, so a single substitution pass over the directory will miss half the files | README.md notes the xlsx is a companion and warns to 'keep one authoritative source', which is a manual discipline with no automated check

concepts.title: Knowledge Vault Subsystem
concepts.description: OKF v0.1 vault tooling: a zero-dependency structural validator, gate tests, starter bundle, and build prompts.
concepts.notes: core executable is knowledge-vault/scripts/validate-vault.mjs, 461 lines, node: builtins only, zero npm dependencies | it locates a vault by finding a directory containing _meta/vault-config.json (or --vault <dir>), reads that config, then walks every .md, .canvas and .base file | flags: --vault <dir>, --allow-broken-links (downgrades broken bundle links and missing manifest files to warnings), --strict-orphans (promotes the no-inbound-links warning to an error), --quiet | exits 1 when errors.length is non-zero, 0 otherwise; always prints a one-line summary of concepts, md files, canvases, errors and warnings | enforced gates: frontmatter required-field contract; description length against max_description_length; timestamp matching ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$; status against the statuses list; domain against the domains list; every tag against the controlled tags vocabulary; resource presence for any type with resource_required; exact H2 section sequence equality against the type's sections array plus exactly one H1; existence on disk of every value in path_fields (resource, sources, docs); okf_version only in the root index.md and only matching the config's value | link discipline: wikilinks forbidden, leading-slash links are errors, repo-host blob/tree/raw URLs are errors, links escaping the repository are errors, and out-of-bundle links outside the '## Citations' H2 are errors except in index files and type 'guide' | any type marked stub:true must carry at least one out-of-bundle or external citation under Citations or it errors | reserved files: log.md must have no frontmatter, must have an H1, and warns without dated '## YYYY-MM-DD' entries; non-root index.md must have no frontmatter | manifest sync against _meta/manifest.json is bidirectional: a manifest id with no file is an error (warning under --allow-broken-links) but a file absent from the manifest is ALWAYS an error, because the manifest is the id allowlist against invented links | max_concept_lines is advisory only and is skipped for free-form types with zero declared sections, such as guide | canvas nodes of type file are resolved against the obsidian vault dir, the bundle, then the repo root, and error if none exists | knowledge-vault/tests/test-validator-gates.sh proves the gates bite: 2 assert_clean cases (the shipped starter bundle, and the bundle after the documented copy-and-rewrite) and 7 assert_error cases covering wikilink, repo-host URL, missing resource path, stub without citation, dangling canvas node, concept missing from the manifest, and a renamed section | knowledge-vault/templates/github/validate-vault.yml is an OPT-IN CI template with {{VAULT_DIR}} and {{MAIN_BRANCH}} tokens, pinning actions/setup-node@v4 at node-version 20 with no install step, and its own header warns that in the origin project the validator 'was wired into no workflow at all' | DOC DRIFT: that warning applies to this repo right now — grep over .github/workflows and package.json finds no reference to validate-vault.mjs or knowledge-vault, so the validator is run by nothing in CI here | this repo's own live vault config is docs/knowledge-vault/_meta/vault-config.json declaring bundle_root docs/knowledge-vault, okf_version 0.1, 5 domains, 4 statuses, 21 tags and 20 types | UNKNOWN: whether docs/knowledge-vault currently contains any concept files or a _meta/manifest.json — only vault-config.json and this build's manifest-parts were observed
